risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: The cardholder's request and the AO's authorization move by memo, note or email with no tracking. A purchase can be made before authorization arrives, or the authorization cannot be found when an auditor asks for it.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: When the AO declines, funds are not available, or the price is unreasonable or over the single transaction limit, the SOP does not say what the cardholder does next. Requests stall or are retried informally.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: A cardholder splits one requirement into several charges to stay under the single transaction limit, and nobody notices until a later review.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: A cardholder accepts online terms that contain automatic renewal, recurring payments or indemnification without spotting them, so the agency is bound to open-ended liability.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: No one is sure who signs for receipt of goods: the AO, the accepting employee, or the purchaser. Invoices reach reconciliation without the required signature.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: The signed paper SOA sits between the cardholder and the AO and misses the 10-workday AO certification deadline.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: The cardholder has to chase another employee for a signature on the invoice and cannot reconcile until it arrives, so the 7-workday deadline slips.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: Transaction data already on the bank SOA is typed again into the core financial accounting system, and keying errors post charges to the wrong accounts.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: Cardholders destroy records too early because one section counts six years from the purchase and another from final payment.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: The cardholder is required to keep a copy of the SOA signed by both cardholder and AO, but the AO sends the signed SOA to FOC and nothing returns a copy to the cardholder.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: The cardholder's AO is on leave during the 3-workday review window, and no one else can certify the SOA.

risks.Title: R12
risks.Description: A cardholder spends weeks trying to resolve a charge with the merchant and passes the 90-day bank dispute window, so the government pays an improper charge.

risks.Title: R13
risks.Description: A merchant refuses to credit a shipping or tax charge, or the bank denies a dispute, and the cardholder has no stated next step.

risks.Title: R14
risks.Description: The cardholder calls the bank but forgets to tell the AO or APC. Nobody checks for fraudulent charges, and no replacement is arranged.

risks.Title: R15
risks.Description: Form A-498 circulates between nominee, Bureau/Office Chief and AO for signatures and gets lost or delayed before the package reaches FOC.

risks.Title: R16
risks.Description: The cardholder's training certificate goes to FOC RDG/TOG with the application but not to the APC, and the APC cannot confirm training before issuing the card.

risks.Title: R17
risks.Description: A temporary credit limit increase is never reversed because no step returns the limit to its original level. Separately, a permanent request from outside OMD has no stated outcome.

risks.Title: R18
risks.Description: Permanent limit increases are never re-reviewed because 'periodic' has no defined interval, and when a limit is no longer needed there is no stated action.

risks.Title: R19
risks.Description: A departing cardholder's account stays open because the APC, the only role that closes accounts, is unavailable or misses the notice.

risks.Title: R20
risks.Description: The cardholder, the AO and the Bureau/Office Chief each assume someone else told the APC about the departure, so no notice arrives before the person leaves.

risks.Title: R21
risks.Description: A departing cardholder waits for account cancellation before handing over records, leaves first, and the files are lost.

risks.Title: R22
risks.Description: Bureaus/Offices sit on the inactive-account list because no deadline or named responder is set, and accounts reported as no longer needed have no closure step.

risks.Title: R23
risks.Description: A cardholder's 3-year refresher lapses unnoticed because nothing reminds them or flags the lapse.

risks.Title: R24
risks.Description: An auditor's document request goes unanswered for weeks because 'timely' is undefined and the cardholder's files are scattered.

risks.Title: R25
risks.Description: An AO leaves before a replacement is named, so cardholders cannot get purchase authorizations and SOAs miss the 10-workday certification.

risks.Title: R26
risks.Description: After an OIG investigation where no disciplinary action is proposed, the case has no closure step. Suspended privileges have no clear test for restoration.

risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: The cardholder and AO/CO plan to the 10-business-day certification deadline and miss the 5-business-day reconciliation deadline. The reverse can also happen, with each party assuming the other has more time.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: The CH's certified statement package with receipts sits with the AO/CO, or comes back to the CH, with no one tracking where it is. As a result, certification misses its deadline or documents are lost.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: The cardholder types each transaction into the NETC 4430/1 log and later compares it line by line with the CitiDirect statement. Typing errors or missed entries create false mismatches or hide real ones.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: The cardholder certifies the quality and quantity of items they bought themselves, so the same person both places the order and confirms receipt. This defeats the required separation of function.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: N4 approves a purchase above the cardholder's single purchase limit, but CITIBANK's authorization system still declines the card at checkout because nobody raised the limit at the bank.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: A purchase request is stopped because funds are not committed, the AO does not approve, the price is not fair and reasonable, the item is on the restricted list, or the bank denies it. The requester never learns what happens next.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: Signed SF 182 copies are sent separately to N4, HRO, N8 and the cardholder, and one copy is late or missed. The cardholder does not know the training can be paid, or HRO receives the form before N4.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: A division prepares an SF 182 for training above $25,000 or not off-the-shelf, and nobody tells them how the training should be bought instead.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: A funding request emailed to N8, or the LOA and document number emailed back, gets buried in an inbox. The cardholder never receives a clear request to buy.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: An unusual request reviewed by the Comptroller or Legal, or a requirement sent to the Comptroller because funds ran out, gets a decision that never returns to N8 or the requestor.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: No one tracks when each participant's two-year refresher, annual ethics or annual CLG 006 training is due. A cardholder or AO is suspended without warning, or keeps using the card while out of compliance.

risks.Title: R12
risks.Description: The A/OPC is out when a cardholder reports fraud, a lost card or a denied transaction. The bank is not contacted 'immediately' and there is no named backup.

risks.Title: R13
risks.Description: A suspect transaction is reported as both a dispute and fraud. The invoice is short-paid twice and the account becomes delinquent.

risks.Title: R14
risks.Description: The cardholder disputes a charge in CitiDirect but the signed paper dispute form is not faxed, is faxed with different details, or is faxed late. CITIBANK then cannot act within the 60-day window.

risks.Title: R15
risks.Description: The AO/CO reports a suspected unauthorized purchase, or a charge is found to be misuse that cannot be disputed. Nothing defines whether certification is held, who investigates, or how the charge is resolved.

risks.Title: R16
risks.Description: When the cardholder is away, the AO reviews and certifies the statement alone. Because the AO and CO are the same person, no second set of eyes checks the transactions until the CH returns, possibly after payment.

risks.Title: R17
risks.Description: The cardholder tells the AO about a lost card, but the AO's written report to the A/OPC is late or missing details such as same-day purchases. The A/OPC cannot confirm what to block or dispute.

risks.Title: R18
risks.Description: A cardholder transfers or retires without the A/OPC finding out in time, and the card stays active after departure.

risks.Title: R19
risks.Description: A departing cardholder's paper transaction files are incomplete or misplaced when turned in. Documents cannot be found during the 10-year retention period when auditors ask.

risks.Title: R20
risks.Description: The semi-annual program review is prepared and approved by the same office, so weaknesses in the A/OPC's own oversight are not independently challenged. If approval is refused, no path is defined.

risks.Title: R21
risks.Description: No one owns forwarding the review package by a known date, or running the suspension and stand-down training after a failed review. The package is late or the corrective actions stall.

risks.Title: R22
risks.Description: The receipt/inspection and acceptance signatures are missing, illegible or come from the cardholder. The AO only finds out when initialing receipts at month end, after the money has been charged.

risks.Title: R23
risks.Description: The sponsoring department forgets to send N4 the final conference bill, or sends the approval request after commitments are made, so N4 cannot match charges to the LOA.

risks.Title: R24
risks.Description: Year-end unfunded requirements are collected through untracked replies. A cardholder buys an item N8 did not approve, or an approved item is missed before funds lapse.

risks.Title: R25
risks.Description: A paid-but-not-received item or a promised warranty credit is forgotten after the cardholder pays in full. The next billing cycle passes and the dispute window closes.

risks.Title: R26
risks.Description: The AO and cardholder identify an item as accountable property but never tell N4. The item is not recorded in DPAS and cannot be tracked.

risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: SBA does not answer within 15 business days. With no follow-up rule, the request can sit unnoticed, or staff may treat the silence as approval and implement the Loan Action without SBA's written approval.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: SBA declines the Servicing Request, and nobody is assigned to tell the Borrower or decide whether to revise, resubmit, or close the request.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: SBA asks for additional information, and the request stalls because no one owns the reply and no deadline applies to it.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: Request details, SBA responses, and call notes are entered in the Computer Tracking System, the Loan File, or both. Each place ends up holding a different partial history of the request.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: A Borrower makes a request by phone or in person and never puts it in writing. The request either sits open indefinitely or is worked without a written request.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: The Lender asks the Borrower and Obligors for financial statements, tax returns, appraisals, lien searches, and other documents. Nothing tracks which items are still outstanding, so the request stalls.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: A financial statement or appraisal that was 'current' when received is stale by the time of the decision. The analysis then rests on outdated numbers.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: A Guarantor or other Obligor refuses or fails to sign consent to a material change. The SOP gives no next step, so the change may go ahead without that consent.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: Loan Documents are modified and executed before the Borrower has cured Defaults, delivered consideration, or every Obligor has consented. In some cases this happens before SBA's written approval is received.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: The Lender wrongly concludes it has unilateral authority and takes the Loan Action without SBA's prior approval or required notice. Alternatively, it sends routine actions to SBA that SBA has asked not to receive.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: The Loan Action Record or credit memo reuses a senior lienholder's analysis, and nobody checks that it is independent.

risks.Title: R12
risks.Description: Staff read the letter rule as allowing partial reliance on a senior lienholder's analysis, while the credit memo rule demands full independence. Submissions end up meeting different standards.

risks.Title: R13
risks.Description: The request is sent to the wrong SBA Loan Center. For example, a liquidation-status Express loan goes to NGPC instead of CLSC, and the response clock effectively starts over.

risks.Title: R14
risks.Description: A modified mortgage or new lien document is never recorded because no one decided it was 'necessary', or because recording has no deadline. The lien priority or perfection is then impaired.

risks.Title: R15
risks.Description: After a Borrower is found not viable, the request is denied, but the 'more appropriate actions' are never started and the Borrower may not be told of the denial.

risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: A clinician or unit learns of a significant adverse event, but no one is named to tell the Risk Manager or told how fast. The Risk Manager hears about it late, so every 'immediately' step and the 24-hour Issue Brief clock start late.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: On a multi-patient event, the notice is relayed person to person by calls or emails with no shared record: Risk Manager, then Chief of Staff or Associate Director, then facility Director, then VISN Director, then the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management. If it stalls at any desk, Central Office receives the Issue Brief after 24 hours.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: Staff disagree about whether the 24-hour limit covers both the facility-to-VISN leg and the VISN-to-Central Office leg, and about who submits. The brief is sent twice, or it is not sent because each party assumes the other did it.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: A minor-harm disclosure is forgotten or happens days later, and nothing shows it, because no record of the event or the disclosure is required.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: A patient's institutional disclosure is held while the Central Office large-scale process runs. Nobody is on record as having judged that the delay is safe, and the patient's care is affected while they wait.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: During an emotional meeting, leaders skip a required element, for example compensation information or notice of the right to outside legal advice, and nobody notices.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: After the meeting, the leaders who held it assume an authorized note author will write the CPRS Institutional Disclosure note. The note is never entered, or it leaves out why the disclosure was not done in person.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: The investigation produces new findings, but neither the Risk Manager nor the leaders take ownership of telling the patient, so the patient is not kept informed.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: The Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health disagrees with the triage or SME Review Panel recommendation, and the case stops because nobody knows whether to re-review, refer elsewhere, or decide directly.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: The CRB reports it lacks enough information and sends a plan and timeline, but the timeline passes with no one reconvening the board.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: The Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management and the SME Review Panel each think the other refers the case and submits the risk report. The Principal Deputy receives two reports, or none.

risks.Title: R12
risks.Description: A case moves among triage, the Principal Deputy, the SME Review Panel, the CRB Chair, and the CRB with no tracker and no deadlines. It sits for weeks at one stage while facilities hold disclosures for affected patients.

risks.Title: R13
risks.Description: After a decision to disclose, field notice, site visit, OGC review, patient letters, clinical follow-up, and the VBA notice are each assumed to be someone else's job. Some patients are not contacted, or are contacted before materials are reviewed.

risks.Title: R14
risks.Description: The look-back finds that harm did not occur or the risk is negligible, but nobody is assigned to tell the already-notified patients, who keep worrying about an exposure that did not happen.

risks.Title: R15
risks.Description: The same disclosure facts already in CPRS notes are hand-compiled by the Risk Manager, retyped into the facility report, and retyped again into the VISN report. Counts drift and reports arrive late.

risks.Title: R16
risks.Description: The facility reports only counts and types, so the VISN cannot fill in the event dates, patient counts, deaths, departments, and triggering events it must report, and has to chase each facility.

risks.Title: R17
risks.Description: Decision records, the CRB vote statement, and the panel report are filed in different places by different offices, and the complete case record cannot be assembled for the After Action Review or legal review.

risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: An employee services equipment with several energy sources. Because the group lockout procedure is not written, one source is left unlocked or one worker's lock is not part of the group, and the equipment starts up while someone is inside.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: The verification check shows the equipment still has energy. The SOP gives no instruction, so the employee may troubleshoot under partial isolation or start work anyway.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: The employee who attached a lock has left the site or ended their shift. A coworker or supervisor cuts or removes the lock without confirming that person is clear, and the equipment is re-energized while they are still exposed.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: An affected employee who was away from the area never hears that the machine was shut down or is about to be re-energized, so they try to run it or walk into it during start-up.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: Locks are removed for a test and nobody records who removed them, when, or whether they were put back. Equipment is left energized after the test while others believe it is still locked out.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: After re-locking, the control check shows the equipment still energizes. The SOP does not say whether to stop, re-isolate, or escalate, so work may resume anyway.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: A contractor arrives and starts work before either side has shared its lockout/tagout procedures. Company employees then do not know which locks or rules apply.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: The contractor's procedure is weaker than the company's, or it conflicts with it (for example on lock types or group lockout). Company employees are told to comply with it and nobody decides which rule wins.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: At shift change the outgoing employee removes their lock before the incoming employee applies theirs. The equipment is briefly unprotected, or the next shift does not know it is locked out.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: The one person assigned to monitor locks during a long-term shutdown is absent or leaves, and a tampered or removed lock goes unnoticed for the rest of the shutdown.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: No one is actually named to do the survey and it is never redone. Tasks judged not to need lockout have no stated alternative control, so they are performed unprotected.

risks.Title: R12
risks.Description: A production supervisor decides a routine task can skip lockout and uses an unverified control circuit. No qualified person signs off the risk assessment or the circuit design before workers rely on it.

risks.Title: R13
risks.Description: Staff read one section saying control circuits never isolate energy and another allowing control circuits as safeguarding, and they apply the wrong rule to an electrical source.

risks.Title: R14
risks.Description: A new or transferred employee is assigned to service equipment before training is finished, because nothing checks the training record at assignment.

risks.Title: R15
risks.Description: Annual retraining dates lapse unnoticed, and the change-based triggers (new assignment, procedure change, new hazard, non-compliance) are never reported to whoever trains.

risks.Title: R16
risks.Description: The annual inspection of some procedures is skipped, or it is done by someone who uses the procedure, because no owner schedules inspections or checks inspector independence.

risks.Title: R17
risks.Description: An inspection finds a procedure is not protecting employees, but retraining and the procedure fix have no owner or deadline. Work continues under the deficient procedure.

risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: A requestor finds that the vendor they want is not on the approved vendor list. The SOP does not say whether the request stops, goes to vendor approval, or proceeds anyway, so a quality-affecting item could be bought from an unevaluated vendor.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: Only the requestor checks the vendor against the approved list. If they skip or misread the check, nothing later in the flow catches it before the order is placed.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: A product fails the compliance review, or Laboratory Management rejects the request. The requestor is not told what to fix or whether to resubmit, so the request is abandoned or quietly resubmitted unchanged.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: No one is named to do the required vendor and product compliance review. Each party assumes someone else did it, and the request reaches Laboratory Management without the review or its record.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: The request passes from requestor to reviewer to Laboratory Management to the DFG purchasing agent with no tracking. It sits in an inbox, and the requestor cannot see where it is.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: The laboratory assumes DFG keeps the purchasing records and DFG assumes the laboratory does, so neither keeps a complete set.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: A calibration service or reference material vendor does not meet MAN-000041 traceability requirements. The SOP does not say the vendor must be rated unacceptable, so it could still go on the list.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: The QSM is the only role that maintains the approved vendor list. When the QSM is away, newly approved vendors are not added and outdated entries are not corrected, and requestors check a stale list.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: Vendor performance tracking and list reviews are never scheduled, so a vendor with repeated problems or a lapsed accreditation stays on the approved list for years.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: It is unclear who owns the periodic review of the vendor list, so the QSM and a laboratory-designated person each assume the other is doing it.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: The receiver hand-writes the receipt date and initials on the receiving record and again on each container, and the two entries may not match or one may be skipped.

risks.Title: R12
risks.Description: A reagent or consumable is put on the shelf after receipt and used in testing before anyone has inspected or verified it, because nothing marks it as on hold.

risks.Title: R13
risks.Description: A delivery is short or contains the wrong item, but the discrepancy does not affect quality. The SOP says nothing about who contacts the vendor or DFG, so the missing items are never chased.

risks.Title: R14
risks.Description: Staff discard material that should have been returned for credit, or return material that should have been destroyed. Different people make inconsistent choices because no role or criteria are defined.

risks.Title: R15
risks.Description: Records of unsatisfactory materials are kept at receiving but never reach the person monitoring vendor performance, so trends go unnoticed.

risks.Title: R16
risks.Description: A vendor recalls a reagent or reference material. The laboratory notes it for the next periodic review instead of immediately pulling the affected stock and reassessing the vendor.

risks.Title: R17
risks.Description: The vendor evaluation passes back and forth between Laboratory Management, unnamed lab staff, and the QSM. The documented outcome or the resulting actions never reach the vendor list.

risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: The fingerprint check or suitability determination comes back unfavorable. Nobody is told what to do next, so the supervisor keeps ordering equipment and messaging a candidate whose offer may not proceed.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: One of the five prerequisites (TSN, ISA, onboarding documents, SAC, suitability) stays open. HRD does not set an EOD, and nobody is assigned to find and chase the missing item, so the start date quietly slips.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: The fingerprints and HRO 1197 are shipped by courier and sit untracked until HRD happens to receive them. A late or lost package goes unnoticed while the EOD cannot be set.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: The supervisor tells the candidate a start date at selection, but HRD sets a different date after clearance. Arrival preparation is then timed to the wrong day.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: The supervisor follows the first-week checklist and submits the network/PIV-exclusion request after the new hire arrives, rather than when the name appears in the GAL. The new hire then has no network access in the first days.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: A missing eAuth or Linc Pass invitation is not noticed until the 14 to 30 day check. That leaves too little of the 30-day grace period to enroll and activate a Linc Pass.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: The supervisor emails the wrong ATAC address about a missing eAuth invitation, and the request is delayed or never handled.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: The 30-day username/password exception expires before the Linc Pass is activated, and the new hire cannot log in. Escalations to ATAC or HRD PSS also have no stated next step.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: Nobody returns the I-9 documents to HRD Minneapolis within three days of the reporting date, because each person assumes someone else will.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: Nobody contacts HR Systems Access or FATA to add the EIN, so the new hire cannot use WebTA or Concur when the first timesheet or trip comes due.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: The Government email address is retyped into EmpowHR with a typo. The eAuth invitation goes to a wrong address and the new hire never receives it.

risks.Title: R12
risks.Description: ISA completion is recorded in several places, and one copy is wrong or missing. As a result, ITD is not alerted to create the email account, or AgLearn shows the training as incomplete.

risks.Title: R13
risks.Description: ITD creates the email address, but nobody tells the Hiring Manager. The Service Now request waits until the manager happens to check the GAL.

risks.Title: R14
risks.Description: Required drug testing or medical clearances are still open when the EOD is set. The new hire could start a position before a required clearance is complete.

risks.Title: R15
risks.Description: Transcripts and drug test results, or the forms of a new hire not using the Onboarding Application, are never collected, because no one is named to collect them.

risks.Title: R16
risks.Description: Requests for a purchase card, fleet PIN, travel card, passport, or international clearance go to separate offices by ad hoc contact, and one stalls with no record that it was made.

risks.Title: R17
risks.Description: The candidate declines or does not respond to the TSN, and the supervisor's reminders and preparations continue with no defined close-out.

risks.Title: R18
risks.Description: The benefits check-ins 'around days 30 and 45' slip, and the new hire misses benefit decisions.

risks.Title: R1
risks.Description: Operations finds an error in the DAR and emails the applicant, but nobody knows how the corrected form comes back or when review restarts. The request sits in limbo, and because contact is optional ('may'), a flawed DAR could also be forwarded to the DAC as is.

risks.Title: R2
risks.Description: The applicant clicks Submit, no confirmation page appears, and the SOP does not say what to do next. The applicant may think the request went through when it did not.

risks.Title: R3
risks.Description: The DAC declines or narrows the requested access, and nobody is told to inform the applicant or record the reason. The applicant keeps waiting and chasing the NTRR team.

risks.Title: R4
risks.Description: The reviewed DAR passes from Operations to the DAC, and then the DAC authorization passes to the Admin, with no tracking. A request can stall in someone's inbox with no one noticing.

risks.Title: R5
risks.Description: The Admin sets up the account with more privileges than the DAC approved, for example Query download access that was not authorized. Nothing in the process checks the result.

risks.Title: R6
risks.Description: Someone without authority signs as the institution's Business Official, and the DAR is accepted because review only checks that the form is accurate and complete.

risks.Title: R7
risks.Description: The applicant does not know how long to wait for the approval email or who 'the NTRR team' is. They either chase too early or wait days without acting.

risks.Title: R8
risks.Description: A new investigator without an existing username and password cannot get past the login step required to request an account. The SOP does not say how to get credentials.

risks.Title: R9
risks.Description: Applicants tick the three privileges the procedure tells them to, even when they actually need Data Submission modules (GUID, Data Dictionary), or they request download access they do not need.

risks.Title: R10
risks.Description: The applicant types their details into the PDF DAR and then types them again in the account fields. The two versions can differ, which leads to review errors.

risks.Title: R11
risks.Description: The DAR goes from the applicant to the Business Official for signature and back by email or paper with no tracking. The signature stalls and the request never starts.

recommendations.Title: A1
recommendations.Reason: A paper form with three signatures is easy to lose. One digital record also captures the training certificate needed before issuance (6.A.3, 6.A.4).

recommendations.Title: A2
recommendations.Reason: These are rule-based signature routings (7.F.1) that currently move by hand.

recommendations.Title: A3
recommendations.Reason: This removes the manual package submission and satisfies both 6.A.4 (to the APC) and 7.F.1 (to FOC).

recommendations.Title: A4
